israel.question: Israel or Palestine?
israel.headline: Middle, leans Israel
israel.headlineWhy: “Middle” because his record points both ways; “leans Israel” because he voted against four of the six resolutions to block arms sales to Israel, has taken pro-Israel PAC money, and tied his two votes to block sales in 2026 to the Iran war and settlements while saying he strongly supports Israel’s right to defend itself.
israel.summary: He voted against all four 2025 resolutions to block arms sales to Israel, then for two in April 2026, saying the weapons might be used in the Iran war or for settlement expansion. He has joined Senate Democratic letters on Gaza humanitarian aid, medical visas for Gazans and West Bank settler violence, and voted for a State Department report on Israel’s human rights record. Pro-Israel PACs gave his campaign $9,500 directly; Track AIPAC counts $104,055, far less than Schumer, Booker or Schiff.

items.text: Voted {vote} on both of Sen. Sanders's April 2025 resolutions to block arms sales to Israel. Both failed.
Voted {vote} on both July 2025 resolutions to block weapons sales and exports to Israel, which most of the Democratic caucus supported. Both failed.
Voted {vote} on both April 2026 resolutions to block arms sales to Israel. Both failed.
Voted {vote} to force a State Department report on Israel's human rights practices (S.Res. 852). It failed {yea}–{nay}; the Democratic caucus voted {cY}–{cN}.
Voted {vote} on taking up H.R. 23, which sanctions the International Criminal Court. It failed {yea}–{nay}; the Democratic caucus voted {cY}–{cN}.
Track AIPAC counts {trackaipac} in pro-Israel lobby money to his campaigns over his career.

items.rx: might be used in Iran or to facilitate further settlement activity
items.text: Explaining his April 2026 votes with Sen. Schiff, said they “strongly support Israel’s right to defend itself” but would vote to block sales of weapons that “might be used in Iran or to facilitate further settlement activity.”
Joined 40 senators calling for a large-scale expansion of humanitarian aid in Gaza and renewed diplomacy to secure a ceasefire.
Joined 41 Democratic colleagues urging the State Department to resume medical and humanitarian visas for civilians in Gaza.

items.rx: reduce violence in the West Bank
items.text: Joined Schumer, Booker and 41 other Democratic senators urging Prime Minister Netanyahu to crack down on settler violence in the West Bank.

On the U.S. strikes on Iran’s nuclear sites, said dismantling Iran’s nuclear program is “essential to Israel’s safety and right to exist,” while faulting the president for acting without congressional authorization.
Pro-Israel PACs gave his campaign {proTotal} directly, all in 2022: AIPAC’s PAC, JACPAC and DMFI PAC (FEC, through {through}).
